title: dedicated: improve fleet autoscaler burst controls + utilization reporting (v14)
author: Sofia Alvarez
description:
Motivation: customers running Redwood Dedicated need tighter, predictable short-term burst behaviour and clearer fleet-level utilization signals for billing and autoscaler tuning. This PR refines the fleet autoscaler burst controls and expands utilization reporting to include per-queue and per-instance ephemeral-burst metrics so operators can reason about burst consumption vs steady-state capacity.

What this PR does: compact summary in one string - adds a configurable burst_token_bucket per pool + eviction logic for long-lived bursts; introduces two new Prometheus metrics (redwood_dedicated_burst_tokens_remaining, redwood_dedicated_ephemeral_burst_usage_total) with labels (pool,region,instance_type,queue); updates the Dedicated autoscaler controller to account for ephemeral burst tokens when making scale-down decisions; surfaces a per-fleet utilization report endpoint (/v1/fleet/utilization?window=1h) returning CSV-friendly rows; adds e2e and unit tests; updates docs and adds a migration note for Dedicated customers.

Implementation notes: burst token bucket is implemented as a lightweight shared in-memory counter backed by the existing scheduler state and checkpointed to Redis for cross-controller failover. Tokens are refilled at pool-level using pool.burst_rate and pool.burst_capacity config. When tokens are exhausted, new burst allocations are denied and requests fall back to queued steady-state slots. The autoscaler now subtracts ephemeral_burst_allocations from available_capacity when calculating safe scale-down targets for stable periods (configurable via autoscaler.scale_down_burst_reserve_pct).

Checklist:
- [x] unit tests for token bucket accounting and refill logic
- [x] integration tests with autoscaler decision loop
- [x] Prometheus metric names and labels reviewed with observability team
- [x] docs updated with migration guidance and examples
- [x] release notes entry

Notes for reviewers: key files are controller/autoscaler/fleet_autoscaler.go, controller/autoscaler/burst_tokens.go, observability/metrics/metrics_definitions.go, api/v1/fleet_utilization.go, docs/dedicated/burst-controls.md. The change touches pathing for Redis checkpoint keys; please pay attention to checkpoint migration (see migration/migrations/20260218_burst_checkpoint.md). This is performance-sensitive: I measured no regression on p95 serving latency in a local perf canary with default configs.

Related: ENG-1429 (fleet autoscaler improvements), ENG-2048 (billing/usage alignment).

Add metrics and fleet utilization endpoint

Final polish: CI fixes and linting
review_comments: Avi Patel: Can you explain how this interacts with autoscaler burst windows? I worry about double-counting capacity.

Sofia Alvarez: The autoscaler uses burst tokens only for ephemeral allocations and explicitly subtracts ephemeral allocations when evaluating scale-down. Added comments and unit tests to demonstrate the difference.
Lauren Kim: Metric cardinality looks ok but please add region label to the two new metrics.
Sofia Alvarez: Added region label and updated observability docs.
Diego Ramirez: There's a potential race in refill goroutine causing negative tokens under heavy contention.
Sofia Alvarez: Fixed race by changing to atomic ops and added stress test (burst_tokens_stress_test.go).
Priya Singh: Please add a release note and indicate the kube-operator migration path.
Sofia Alvarez: Added migration doc + release notes entry.
release_notes: Added per-pool burst controls and enhanced fleet utilization reporting. Operators can now configure burst capacity and observe ephemeral burst consumption via new Prometheus metrics. Migration: checkpoint keys are updated; follow migration/migrations/20260218_burst_checkpoint.md for upgrade steps.
notes_for_ops: To enable new metrics and migration, upgrade controller to v2026.02.26 and ensure Redis checkpointing is enabled. Update helm values: dedicated.pool.burst_rate and dedicated.pool.burst_capacity if you want non-default burst behaviour.
